div.head: II As 14.1
div.ab: ⁊ gif se mynetere fúl wurðe, slea mon of þa hond, ðe he ðæt fúl mid worhte, ⁊ sette up on ða mynetsmiððan; ⁊ gif hit þonne tyhtle sy, ⁊ he hine ladian wille, ðonne ga he to þam hatum isene ⁊ ladige þa hond, mid ðe mon tyhð, ðæt he þæt facen mid worhte; ⁊ gif he on þam ordale ful wurðe, dó mon þæt ilce, swa hit ær beforan cwæð.

Gif se mynetere ful wurþe, slea mon ða hand of, ðe þæt ful mid worhte, ⁊ sette ufan on ða minetsmiþan. Gif hit ðonne tyhtle sy, ⁊ he hine ladian wille, ðonne gá he to hatum isene ⁊ ladie ða hand, mid ðæm mon tyhþ, þæt he þæt facn worhte. Gif he ðonne on ðæm ordale ful wurþe, dó man þæt ylce, swa hit her beforan cwyþ.

[Gif se] mynetere ful wurðe, slea man ða hand of, ðe he þæt ful [mid wor]hte, ⁊ sette upp an þa mynetsmyðþan. Gif hit þonne [tyhtle] sie, ⁊ he hine ladian wille, þonne ga he to hatum isene ⁊ ladie [þa hand, m]id þe man tyhð, þæt þæt facen worhte. Gif he þonne on þam or[dale ful] wurþe, do man þæt ylce swa hit her beforan cweð.

Si monetarius reus fuerit, amputetur eius (ei) manus et ponatur supra monete fabricam. Si inculpatio sit, et se purgare uelit, eat ad ferrum calidum et allegiet manum que inculpatur (adcausatam) quod falsum fecerit. Si in ordalio reus fuerit, fiat ei quod supra dictum est.

⁊ gif se mynetere fúl wurðe, slea mon of þa hond, ðe he ðæt fúl mid worhte, ⁊ sette up on ða mynetsmiððan; ⁊ gif hit þonne tyhtle sy, ⁊ he hine ladian wille, ðonne ga he to þam hatum isene, ⁊ ladige þa hond, mid ðe mon tyhð, ðæt he þæt facen mid worhte; ⁊ gif he on þam ordale ful wurðe, dó mon þæt ilce, swa hit ær beforan cwæð.

(Und H) wenn der Münzer [der Fälschung] schuldig ertappt wird, haue man die Hand ab, mit der er die Fälschung verübt hat und befestige [sie] (oben Ld) über der Münzschmiede; (und H) wenn es dagegen [nur] Anklage ist, und er sich [davon] reinigen will, dann gehe er zum heissen Eisen[ordal] und reinige die Hand, mit welcher er verklagt ist, dass er die Fälschung damit verübt habe; (und H) wenn er (aber So Ld) in diesem Ordal schuldig erscheint, thue man [ihm] dasselbe, wie es eben (hier Ot Ld) zuvor lautet(e H).

(And, H) if the moneyer is caught guilty [of forgery], let the hand be struck off with which he committed the forgery and fastened (up, Ld) over the mint; (and, H) if on the other hand it is [only] an accusation, and he wishes to clear himself [of it], then let him go to the hot iron [ordeal] and clear the hand with which he is accused of having committed the forgery; (and, H) if (however, So Ld) he is found guilty in this ordeal, let the same be done [to him] as it just (here, Ot Ld) said above.

And if a moneyer is found guilty [of issuing base or light coins] the hand shall be cut off with which he committed the crime, and fastened up on the mint. But if he is accused and he wishes to clear himself, then shall he go to the hot iron [ordeal] and redeem the hand with which he is accused of having committed the crime. And if he is proved guilty the same punishment shall be inflicted as we have already declared.

And if a moneyer is convicted, the hand with which he committed the crime is to be struck off, and put up on the mint. And if, however, there is an accusation, and he wishes to clear himself, he is then to go to [the ordeal of] hot iron, and redeem the hand with which he is accused of having committed the crime; and if he is convicted at the ordeal, the same is to be done as it said here above.

Die Handhaftigkeit ergibt der Ggs. zu ‘Anklage’ 3 Z. weiter. — Diesen Satz benutzt IV Atr 5, 3
That the offender is taken in the act follows from the contrast with ‘accusation’ 3 ll. further on. — This sentence is used by IV Atr 5, 3

Ebd. Spiegelnde Strafe 2. Verderbend ändert Will. Malmesbur. über Dunstan (ed. Stubbs 300), bzw. G. pontif. 27 diese Strafe in Hand- und Fussabhauen oder Tod, den freilich die Verstümmelung (s. d. Gl 4) oft nur ersetzte

Ibid. Spiegelnde Strafe 2. Will. Malmesbur., on Dunstan (ed. Stubbs 300), or G. pontif. 27, corruptly changes this punishment into cutting off of hand and foot, or death, for which, admittedly, mutilation (see that word in Gl 4) was often merely a substitute

Volles (dreifaches) Ordal (s. d. Gl 23 a. 33 d; Eisen 10 A) fordert als Reinigung IV Atr 5, 2 (III 8). — Zu den letzten Wörtern des §: in ähnlichen Wendungen überwiegt swa hit her ær beforan (bufan) cwið, cweð, cyð, segð, sægð; doch kommt auch sæde vor; Pogatscher in Anglia 23, 296

The full (threefold) ordeal (see that word in Gl 23 a. 33 d; Eisen 10 A) is required as exculpation by IV Atr 5, 2 (III 8). — On the last words of the §: in similar phrases swa hit her ær beforan (bufan) cwið, cweð, cyð, segð, sægð predominates; but sæde also occurs; Pogatscher in Anglia 23, 296
